what: Draws the video on a three canvas in the same spot and smears it in the direction of travel by the scroll (or supplied) speed — the shader samples one point 12 times along that direction and averages (blur = speed × .012, max .14) the faster you wind, the longer the trail, and when it stops it sharpens by .2 each step. With key on, the background is removed by the difference from the corner color (.035~.14) so only the product stands out

options.smear: Share that spreads at speed 1, default .012
options.max: Largest spread (share of panel size), default .14
options.key: If true, treats the corner color as the background and keys it out — for product videos with a solid background
options.drive: For an event, it uses the fx:velocity (detail.velocity) sent to the element instead of window scroll — when passing along the fx:time speed of the wheel stage (wheel-time-stage)
options.video: Child <video>(muted·loop·playsinline) — used only as a texture and hidden

from.where: index.js product ring · usage scene plate — spreads in the blade direction by the speed of wheel winding, and the ring video has its background removed (original WebGL video plate)

note: window.THREE must exist (load three-global.js before three.cjs, as in the demo). On a page opened via file://, the browser blocks reading the video into WebGL (cross-origin), so only the video shows, without the blur — serve it over http. Without WebGL, only the video shows as well
